reviews.review: Fun progression. No PvP makes this game enjoyable and peaceful compared to PvEvP.

Fun fact: This game is published by Bilibili. Hope to see Bilibili release more high-quality games in the future!

Keep in mind that I'm not a professional reviewer and I very well may have missed things. I'm a casual gamer, so this reflects my opinions as someone who plays for fun and not to deliberately find things to talk about.

This game was gifted to me, so I went in with no real expectations and didn't know what was awaiting me. Only thing I knew was that it's an extraction shooter, inspired by Tarkov (duh). It should be disclosed that I have not nearly reached endgame. I'm barely even level 10 yet. Regardless, I've discovered enough that I feel confident in posting about it. I will leave some things out though, as I think they are more fun to experience without having been told about them. Cons and pros aside, I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a pure PvE experience and doesn't mind some lack of immersion. It's like a cozy game with intense elements. Lots of fun and lots of cool factor.

I have a few select mods installed for quality of life, and I suggest looking into them. However, do NOT install the coop mod.

[h2] So, pros... [/h2]
The gameplay loop is nice. Repeatability works. Looping yourself around every day is alright, you always have something to do. Sleeping is not a painfully structured activity that has conditions; you sleep when you sleep, and you choose exactly how long you wanna sleep. As someone who is not very patient, this is a godsend.

Raids feel more like matches, but inversed. Rather than, like in Tarkov, a raid being more like a detached situation from being in the hideout, Duckov is more like the bunker being a part of the game world, and exiting from and entering into it is quite seamless and fast. It makes it feel like you're actually living in it, and not transferring between two worlds.

Quests are simple and easy; they are explained well and don't drag on about lore that nobody asked for. It's not particularly immersive, but it's refreshing to see a game where quests are designed to progress you through the game and nudge you into discovering content and areas, rather than try to be something they aren't (I don't like quests that try to sound important when it's clear that they're just for progression - yes, I'm looking at you Jaeger).

Weapon diversity is diverse enough that calibers matter, but not advanced enough that different calibers will make or break your gunfights. This gun takes this bullet, that gun takes that bullet, enough said. More rare guns can still take the same caliber as one of your early game rifles, which means less nonsense saving money for ammo, and more time actually using them for their purpose.

Bunker areas are cool. I've not unlocked them all yet though. They look good and are well designed. Easily usable and easily recognizable. The fact some have traders is neat and gives some variety. I still have no idea what the garage / van room is for yet, so take this... as it is. Visually cool, so I think of it as a pro. The fact you can extract from and enter into Ground Zero from two different places from within the bunker is cool, and very useful. Provides some variety.

Bots are fine, perhaps overpowered in some situations. Some are really stupid, some are incredibly insane. It does provide some diversity, and it's very easy to pick people apart. PMCs have cool loot and cool gear. The fact you can get ganged up on by living mushrooms is wild and hilarious.

Skill enhacements and area upgrades are fine. Nothing special really. Very clearly outlined requirements, fair spacing between upgrade tiers. Level requirements are kinda silly, but I understand the purpose; this comes from someone who does not like level-based upgrades.

The way you explore new maps is cool, and gives it an adventurous experience. Extract points are also pretty cool, where you can choose whether to extract from a zone or just walking back home.

Cute ducks. Cute running animations. Hotkeyable quack voiceline is +1

Pet doggo is +1. He be a bouncy boi. You can store things on his back. Very neat, it took me a while to understand how that works. His backpack capacity can be upgraded.

[h2] And the cons... [/h2]
Hitboxes are really strange on some maps. Some objects have a solid 1-1.5m hitbox outside of the object itself, so I find myself walking into a wall attempting to follow an object's edges. It's annoying but can be ignored once you learn the map.

Aiming around corners is painful if you're like me and you are better at aiming on a flat 2D surface than isometrically. Top down doesn't really help this issue, and I am well aware that it's a skill issue. Regardless, it's annoying. Not much can be done about it, I'm pointing it out as it's relevant to Duckov.

Dive rolling movement is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, excuse the language. It locks the character up and you cannot move dynamically until the roll is over and it has reset the animation. This has killed me more than once. In my opinion this has to be redone in order to make it a fluent feature and not a half-baked attempt at dodging. Also, being able to dive-roll while reloading - effectively cancelling the reload - is annoying. This has almost killed me a number of times; I rely on muscle memory a lot.

The UI is way too big. Unlike in Tarkov, where the inventory size feels adequate and easy to look at and read, Duckov's inventory UI is really, really big. On a 1440p 32" display, trying to quickly sort my inventory becomes a pain. Everything is big and has effects that detract from the experience. I don't have eye conditions (no dyslexia, dizziness or disorientation of any kind) and I still find that the size of the inventory to cause a mild headache from time to time. It would be nice with a scale slider.
Quest pages from traders should, in my opinion, be on In-Progress by default, with the first quest being selected. Having to manually select stuff just to re-read a requirement or condition gets tiring.

Quick move does not move items to the selected page of your backpack/warehouse section. It's very annoying, but if you're addicted or used to manually moving individual items then this will be just fine for you. It's only an issue if you want to sort items per page. Also, a nitpick, but quick move being bound to F and not used with a modifier (i.e Shift + Left Mouse) is a bit annoying. I had to google it, but once I found out how it works it became easy to do. It's not a dealbreaker.

Being unable to move bunker areas post-creation sucks, so if you make a mistake you cannot rectify it. It's not a game breaking thing, but it could've been done better. Plan ahead if misalignment or geometric things bother you, and don't rush creation.

The transition wallpaper / loading screen feels uncreative, I think it could use some more in-depth artwork. It has the default Unity Engine designer font, and as an ex-game dev this bothers me. The animated wallpaper is nice, but that's about it. Give it some proper love please.

If any Duckov dev reads this, know that this is written out of a love for the game and a wish for it to be improved upon. There's good potential in this game, and I have high hopes for it.

I will now resume my playthrough, thanks for reading this far! I give this game a solid 9.5/10

Picked this up a few days ago and honestly — it’s an absolute time killer (in the best possible way).

[h3] What Works [/h3]

This game is a fantastic mix of Escape From Tarkov-style RPG elements and a much more relaxed, accessible atmosphere.

[h3] It captures that familiar Tarkov feeling: [/h3]

[list]
    [*]Solid progression system
    [*]Stash fills up quickly
    [*]The items you actually need are never the ones you find
    [*]Constant “one more run” mentality
    [*]Visually, it’s not perfect — but it’s very close. The art style is clean, readable, and charming in its own way. It doesn’t try to be hyper-realistic, and that works in its favor.
    [*]The progression loop feels satisfying. You’re always working toward something, and the balance between loot pressure and chill gameplay is handled really well.
    [*]And as a big bonus — [b]it runs perfectly on Linux.[/b] Smooth performance, no weird issues, no tinkering required. Always great to see games that just work.
[/list]

[h3] What Could Be Improved [/h3]

A few things I’d personally love to see:

[list]
    [*]A broader variety of contemporary US/EU weapon platforms would add more flavor. TT and PM are iconic, but they weren’t my personal favorites in Tarkov.
    [*]Bunker customization could go further. Adding posters like in Tarkov would be a great touch. Imagine some “PlayDuck” posters on the wall — that would add personality and humor.
[/list]

[h3] Final Thoughts [/h3]

If you like Tarkov’s core loop but want something less stressful and more approachable, this is a brilliant spin on the formula.
